newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria urges Zaire and Rwanda to dialogue.
newsitem.headline: Algeria urges Zaire and Rwanda to dialogue.

text.p: Algeria on Thursday urged Rwanda and Zaire to halt hostilities and search for a negotiated settlement for the conflict in the African Great Lakes area.

"Aware of the dangers and threats which this situation is weighing down peace, security and stability in all the region, Algeria invites the brother countries, Rwanda and Zaire, to show a sense of responsibility and self-control," the Algerian foreign ministry said in a statement.

The Algerian government was in close contact with several leaders of the region as well as with the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) to promote a lasting political solution to the crisis in the region, it said.
Foreign Minister Ahmed Attaf phoned OAU's Secretary-General Ahmed Salim and sent a message to the foreign ministry of Cameroon, current OAU chairman, the statement said.
Algeria also urged the international community to save hundreds of thousands of refugees uprooted by the new conflict, said the statement carried by the official Algerian news agency (APS).

Fighting between Zairean troops and Tutsi rebels raged near the eastern city of Goma on Thursday and aid agencies responsible for feeding more than a million Hutu refugees prepared to evacuate, aid officials said.
A swathe of eastern Zaire close to Rwanda and Burundi is now outside government control after a lightning campaign by Tutsi guerrillas and the future of Zaire as a unified state is now in doubt.
On Thursday Ahmed Salim held an emergency meeting with aides in Ethiopia's capital Addis Ababa to discuss the Zaire conflict, officials said.
